paragraphs: Abba bar Chanina: Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin, chapter 8, halakhah 4.
Rav Ada son of Rabbi Chanina: [Nedarim 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.22b.3).
Rabbi Gamliel son of Rabbi Chanina: Kohelet Rabbah 5:12.
Rabbi Chama bar Chanina: [Berakhot 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.5b.23); Dikdukei Soferim there, at 32b, reads Rabbi Chiyya bar Chanina.
Rabbi Yehudah bar Chanina: Eruvin 11b (the name appears at [Eruvin 11a:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11a.19)).[^4]
Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina: [Bava Kamma 39a:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.39a.9).

Rabbi Yirmeyah son of Rabbi Chanina: Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 4, halakhah 1. Mareimar bar Chanina: [Bava Metzia 97a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.97a.11). Rava bar Chanina: [Shabbat 19b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.19b.3). Rabbah bar Chanina: [Bava Batra 113b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.113b.3).
Rabbi Tanchum bar Chanina: Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, chapter 4, halakhah 4.[^3]

notes.text: The chapter/halakhah Eruvin, Shabbat and Berakhot locations are Jerusalem Talmud. All fourteen supplied list units, Rav/Rabbi titles, bar/son forms and Chama/Chiyya variants remain distinct; no target identities are bound.

The supplied fourteen list units collectively contain several patronymics, not one demonstrated father or one set of resolved identities. Berakhot 5b directly supplies Chama son of Chanina; exact DKS alternatives remain Hyman-attributed.
The list groups patronymics. The consulted Berakhot passage gives Chama son of Chanina in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak. Hyman’s reported Dikdukei Soferim variant retains its separate locator.

The two Shabbat entries represent alternative attributions within one passage, through Rabbi Achi or Rabbi Yaakov, each described as son of Rabbi Chanina. In Eruvin, Resh Lakish names Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Chanina at the end of 11a. His teaching about a vine partition continues at [Eruvin 11b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11b.1).
